purpose: Throwaway synthetic test of a naive repeated-Rust time-exit idea; not strategy evidence
method: Simulate, inspect filled trade entry bars, add the earliest missing timed exit to a static exit frame, and resimulate until no new exit is added, with a hard iteration cap. Default vectorbt signal conflict behavior is unchanged.

conflict_case.change: Add another A entry signal at bar 2, when its timed exit is due.
conflict_case.result: A remains open; the naive termination check incorrectly sees no new exit to add.

bounded_scaling_probe.scope: Synthetic input, revised retry method, not a trading or performance study
bounded_scaling_probe.limits: Single short run on this host; capped at 250 simulations or 12 seconds. No reference comparison, long-window or realistic-grid benchmark; elapsed time is not a performance guarantee.

longer_scaling_probe.scope: Synthetic input, revised retry method, not a trading or performance study
longer_scaling_probe.limits: Stopped after 12 seconds without convergence. Candidate bar-column pairs are not a count of trades or independent orders. Single run; no reference comparison or valid timing extrapolation to a real walk-forward grid.

group_batched_scaling_probe.scope: Same synthetic setup as longer_scaling_probe, but add the earliest candidate per independent cash group on each rerun
group_batched_scaling_probe.limits: Stopped without convergence. The two capped probes did not reach final results and are not an end-to-end speedup comparison. Group-batching correctness was tested only on small synthetic examples against the Numba callback.

all_candidates_recomputed_probe.scope: Same synthetic setup as longer_scaling_probe, but recompute all currently overdue exit signals each iteration and stop at a stable signal frame
all_candidates_recomputed_probe.callback_order_comparison: idx, col, side, size, price and fees matched within 1e-10 relative and absolute tolerance
all_candidates_recomputed_probe.limits: Single synthetic run; timer excludes the subsequent Numba callback comparison. The earlier capped method did not converge, so this is not an end-to-end speedup measurement. Iteration cycles, behavior outside the tested cases and realistic-grid performance remain unresolved.

all_candidates_larger_grid_probe.scope: Synthetic setup as longer_scaling_probe with 20 independent groups instead of five; recompute all candidate exits each iteration
all_candidates_larger_grid_probe.callback_order_comparison: idx, col, side, size, price and fees matched within 1e-10 relative and absolute tolerance
all_candidates_larger_grid_probe.limits: Single synthetic run; timer excludes data generation and Numba callback comparison. No measured peak memory, multiple-seed performance distribution, intraday OHLC, partial fill or realistic strategy grid. Stability is not guaranteed.

all_candidates_48_group_probe.scope: Synthetic setup as longer_scaling_probe with 48 independent groups instead of five; recompute all candidate exits each iteration
all_candidates_48_group_probe.callback_order_comparison: idx, col, side, size, price and fees matched within 1e-10 relative and absolute tolerance
all_candidates_48_group_probe.limits: Single synthetic run; timer excludes data generation and Numba callback comparison. RSS includes Python baseline and earlier allocations. No multiple-seed performance distribution, intraday OHLC, partial fills or full historical-symbol strategy grid. Stability is not guaranteed.

all_candidates_wide_group_probe.scope: Synthetic setup as longer_scaling_probe, but use 500 columns per group and a 0.002 cash fraction for sizing
all_candidates_wide_group_probe.callback_order_comparison: idx, col, side, size, price and fees matched within 1e-10 relative and absolute tolerance
all_candidates_wide_group_probe.limits: Single synthetic run; 0.002 is the fraction passed to percent sizing, not a percentage point. Timer excludes data generation and Numba callback comparison. RSS includes Python baseline. No multiple-seed performance distribution, intraday OHLC, partial fills or 48-group 500-symbol strategy grid. Stability is not guaranteed.

limitations: These are two invented cases, not a general correctness or performance test.
Price stops, fills with slippage, missing bars, partial fills, retries, many groups and same-bar ordering are untested.
Suppressing a conflicting entry might address this specific example but needs independent testing and does not prove a viable engine implementation.
The current ggTrader time-stop implementation is unchanged.

all_candidates_dense_entry_probe.scope: Synthetic fixed-point Rust reruns, one symbol, no market data; not a strategy test
all_candidates_dense_entry_probe.setup: Constant close 100; entry true on every bar; no ordinary exit or price stop; one shared cash pool; percent size 1.0; zero fees and slippage; time limit one bar. Recompute the full forced-exit mask from each run until unchanged.
all_candidates_dense_entry_probe.interpretation: In this constructed case, required reruns grew with bar count. An arbitrary small fixed cap would refuse a valid-looking case; a large cap may be expensive on wider grouped histories.
all_candidates_dense_entry_probe.limitations: One symbol and one constructed signal pattern; no callback comparison in this probe, no peak-memory measurement, no real-history estimate, no proof of general convergence or complexity. Timing is host-specific.
